core.title: Report each wagon's coupling complexity and flag those above the soft threshold
core.given: A plan whose wagons declare produce/consume artifacts, forming a directed wagon graph keyed on artifact names.
core.when: You plan or validate the plan, including unchanged plans and threshold-only configuration changes.
core.then: Report every wagon's coupling complexity (fan_in x fan_out over the produce->consume name graph) and flag, as advisory and non-blocking, each wagon whose coupling complexity strictly exceeds the configured soft threshold (calibration default 6).
prefer: Run plan validation so each wagon's complexity is visible while planning.
fan_in = wagons consumed from; fan_out = wagons consuming its outputs; reason on the product (Henry-Kafura).
avoid: Blocking or halting planning on the advisory.
Keying coupling on optional contract declarations instead of artifact names.
Renaming/merging artifact names only to lower the product.
core.why: High fan_in x fan_out marks an entangled wagon that hurts separability; non-blocking reporting keeps complexity visible until the threshold is calibrated.
evidence: Plan-validation output reports coupling complexity for every wagon, with advisory findings only for wagons whose fan_in x fan_out strictly exceeds the configured threshold.
The validation run's exit status is unaffected by coupling-complexity findings (advisory, non-blocking).
verification: Compute coupling complexity from the directed wagon graph built on produce/consume artifact names (not optional contract declarations): fan_in = number of distinct wagons a wagon consumes from; fan_out = number of distinct wagons that consume its outputs; proxy = fan_in x fan_out (Henry-Kafura).

Report the proxy for every wagon on every plan-validation run, including unchanged plans; emit an advisory finding only when the proxy strictly exceeds the configured soft threshold (calibration default 6).
Non-blocking enforcement: advisory disposition only, never blocks or fails the run; severity 2; exit status is unaffected.
Promotion to a hard threshold or strict disposition is deferred to corpus calibration.

values: wagon produce/consume artifact name added, removed or renamed

fires: A plan-validation run covers any plan, including an unchanged existing plan: every wagon's fan_in x fan_out is reported.
A planner adds a consume entry that raises a wagon's fan_in x fan_out above the threshold (default 6): reported and flagged advisory.
Only the coupling-complexity threshold setting is changed in configuration: all wagons re-reported and flags recomputed against the new cutoff.
A wagon's product is at or below the threshold: still reported, but no advisory flag (reporting still fires).
doesNotFire: Work that involves neither a wagon graph nor plan validation (for example, editing application code outside planning).
Deciding whether to block or halt planning: this rule never fires as a blocker.

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's command that runs plan validation; the coupling-complexity reporter runs inside it on every invocation, and its output is where the per-wagon report and advisory findings appear.

neutralityNotes: Plan-domain vocabulary (wagon, wagon manifest, produce/consume artifact, plan validation, planner configuration) is treated as framework-level rather than stack-level and is kept in the core; the profile vocabulary itself models wagons and plan artifacts stack-neutrally (layout.wagon_dir, layout.plan_item). The concrete plan-validation command is delivered through enforcement.runner, the only profile key needed. Three kinds of content could not be made neutral and stay bunOnly: (a) the rule-specific planner configuration key name planner.wagon.coupling_complexity_threshold (the core says 'configured soft threshold' but keeps the calibration default 6 so the obligation is identical); (b) the finding id of this rule; (c) the wagon-manifest schema detail 'nullable contract field', generalized in the core to optional contract declarations. Severity 2 and the advisory disposition are per-rule enforcement facts and live in core:verification, not in a profile key.
